audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

I mercati asiatici hanno chiuso con risultati misti; il Nikkei ha chiuso in rialzo del 2.53%, mentre Shanghai è sceso dello 0.73%.

MERCATI OCCIDENTALI: nella seduta precedente, S&P 500 in rialzo dello 0.22%, VIX in calo del 2.67%, DXY in descenso dello 0.11%. L'oro ha guadagnato lo 1.36% raggiungendo i $4560.5/oz, il petrolio è sceso del 1.77% a $92.05 Il rendimento del US 10Y è sceso dello 0.04% al 4.45%.

GEOPOLITICA: La Russia sta sovraspendendo per la guerra in Ucraina, secondo quanto riportato.

MACRO E BANCHE CENTRALI: nessun dato macro rilevante in uscita oggi. Il governatore de Pascale ha criticato i fondi di coesione per l'energia.

Mentre le borse mondiali osservano la consueta pausa festiva, i riflettori restano accesi sul comparto digitale, che continua a operare 24 ore su 24

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. 
  Bitcoin si mantiene sopra i settantatremila dollari con una lieve flessione del 0,17%. 
  I flussi degli ETF hanno registrato una significativa uscita netta di circa 223 milioni di dollari. 
  Questo movimento potrebbe essere influenzato dalle recenti dinamiche del mercato.

  Tra le altcoin, Ethereum guadagna lo 0,39% arrivando a duemilatrecento dollari, mentre Solana cresce dello 0,06% a ottantadue dollari e ventisei centesimi. 
  BNB invece mostra un significativo aumento del 5,34% arrivando a seicentosettanta dollari e trentasei centesimi.

  Il Fear & Greed Index è a 23, in zona di Extreme Fear, il che suggerisce cautela tra gli investitori.

Nessun dato macro in agenda oggi. Per approfondire i temi di oggi, sulla nostra piattaforma trovate gli articoli completi nella sezione Storie in Primo Piano. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani.
audio_script_en:
Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing. 

The Asian markets closed with mixed results; the Nikkei closed up 2.53%, while Shanghai fell by 0.73%.

WESTERN MARKETS: in the previous session, S&P 500 up 0.22%, VIX down 2.67%, DXY down 0.11%. Gold gained 1.36% reaching $4560.5/oz, oil fell 1.77% to $92.05 The US 10Y yield fell 0.04% to 4.45%.

GEOPOLITICS: Russia is overspending for the war in Ukraine, according to reports.

MACRO AND CENTRAL BANKS: no relevant macro data out today. Governor de Pascale criticized cohesion funds for energy.

While global stock markets observe the usual festive pause, the spotlight remains on the digital sector, which continues to operate 24/7

Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets... 
  Bitcoin stays above seventy-three thousand dollars with a slight decline of 0.17%. 
  ETF flows have recorded a significant net outflow of about $223 million. 
  This movement could be influenced by recent market dynamics.

  Among altcoins, Ethereum gains 0.39% reaching $2,300, while Solana grows 0.06% to $82.26 
  BNB instead shows a significant increase of 5.34% reaching $670.36

  The Fear & Greed Index is at 23, in Extreme Fear zone, which suggests caution among investors.

No macro data on the agenda today. To delve deeper into today's topics, find the full articles on our platform in the Top Stories section. Thanks for your attention and see you tomorrow.

articles.title: Contriving Imaginary Gaps in Nuclear Deterrence
articles.snippet: Among some nuclear strategists, military officers, and lawmakers, a belief bordering on the canonical has taken root that the United States is on the short end of a “deterrence gap” with Russia and China. Both countries, and especially Russia, possess theater-range nuclear weapons, whose comparatively small yield is thought to lower the threshold for their use. The relative dearth of these capabilities on the American side, so the thinking goes, denies Washington the ability to answer a limited regional nuclear strike with a comparable response and thus deter such an attack in the first place. articles.title: Project Aperta: enabling cross-border interconnectivity through open finance interoperability
articles.snippet: Project Aperta, led by the Bank for International Settlements (BIS), has been designing, developing and testing a prototype for cross-border open finance interconnectivity via application programming interfaces (APIs) – a "network of networks" that connects existing domestic networks through a neutral interoperability layer. The prototype connects the open finance networks of the United Kingdom, the United Arab Emirates, Brazil, Hong Kong SAR and India.

articles.title: Central Banking in an Age of Global Supply Shocks
articles.snippet: The core assumptions underlying the decades-old inflation-targeting orthodoxy have proven to be unfit for a geopolitically fragmented world characterized by frequent supply-side disruptions. Under such conditions, central banks' traditional monetary policies are only as effective as markets believe them to be.

articles.title: Kansas Fed Pres Warns Oil Price Shock Might Not Be Transitory
articles.snippet: Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City President Jeffrey Schmid has warned that the current global energy shock cannot simply be dismissed as transitory, given already-elevated baseline inflation. Speaking at a conference in Iceland, Schmid pointed out that inflation has stalled near 3% and remained above the Fed's 2% target for a long time, making it challenging for the central bank to "look through’’ surging oil prices. Schmid has argued that current monetary policy may not be restrictive enough, reinforcing his hawkish stance on monetary…

articles.title: India's Central Bank Warns Oil Shock Threatens Growth
articles.snippet: India's economy remains resilient to the external shocks, but the oil price surge amid the global supply disruption poses near-term downside risks to economic growth and upside risks to inflation, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said in its Annual Report for 2025-26 published on Friday. "Against the backdrop of a moderate global growth, the outlook for the Indian economy in 2026-27 remains positive, supported by strong macroeconomic fundamentals, although a prolonged West Asia conflict may pose downside risk," economists at India's central bank…
